report_page.intro: CGM Report. A report of the continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data received from the glucose sources. The CGM Report shows the standardized metrics and glucose profile recommended for the Ambulatory Glucose Profile (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2013). The most recent 14 days, extended on request to 30 days, 90 days or 6 months. Full days ending at the last midnight; consensus ranges only. Available on screen, as a PDF and, optionally, printed.

strategy.change.about.personal:
- **Change Over Time:** for each measure, the value of the 14 days ending at each of the last 26 week ends (line; the weeks are counted back from the time of calculation, not calendar weeks) and the 7-day value of the same weeks (faint dots, shown without comparison: 7 days is shorter than the 14 days the consensus recommends; Battelino et al., 2019), calculated hourly. The table compares the last 4 weeks with 9–13 and 22–26 weeks ago. A 14-day or 7-day value or a 4-week period with less than 70% sensor active has no value (--- in the table, a gap in the line); the differences and the direction are calculated for every period with at least 70% sensor active, and the sensor-active row of the table shows the sensor active of each period that has enough data. GMI is shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2018). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
- **Direction:** whether the last 4 weeks are higher or lower than 22–26 weeks ago (or 9–13 weeks ago when 22–26 weeks ago has less than 70% sensor active), or *No change* when the difference rounds to zero; a numerical difference without clinical interpretation. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. The custom goal is shown separately.
- **Backgrounds of the charts:** green within the custom goal, red outside it, divided exactly at it; neutral gray where no goal is set or no goal can be set.

strategy.custom.intro:
This page uses **the custom ranges and custom goals** in the settings (listed on [Settings Status]({settings_url})). {custom_statement} By default, the tight range is that of Battelino et al. (2023); no goal is set by default for time in tight range or GMI, for which no published target exists.

**In use:** {ranges}: very low below {very_low}, low below {low}, tight range {tight_low}–{tight_high}, high above {high}, very high above {very_high} {unit}; goals: {goals}.

With the default ranges, the values on this page correspond to those on *Consensus Ranges*. With custom ranges or goals, no published target applies to them.
strategy.cx.above: **Time above range.** The 2019 international consensus sets the targets for time above range at less than 25% above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and less than 5% above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L), which are less than 6 hours and less than 1 hour and 12 minutes per day (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3). The 25% target covers levels 1 and 2 together and so includes the time above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). The 2019 consensus defines level 1 hyperglycemia as 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L) and level 2 as above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). This explains the targets in the rows of the time above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L).
strategy.cx.active: **Sensor active (data received by GlucoCraft).** Close to, but not the same as, the CGM system's own figure: only the readings received are counted.
strategy.cx.below: **Time below range.** The 2019 international consensus sets two targets for time below range: less than 4% of the time below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and less than 1% below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3). The 4% target covers levels 1 and 2 together, so it includes the time below 54 mg/dL ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). In a 24-hour day, 4% is 57.6 minutes and 1% is 14.4 minutes; the consensus expresses the targets as less than 1 hour and less than 15 minutes per day (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3). The consensus classifies 54–69 mg/dL (3.0–3.8 mmol/L) as level 1 hypoglycemia and below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) as level 2 (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2); the 2017 consensus describes level 1 as an alert value and level 2 as clinically significant hypoglycemia (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4). This explains the targets in the rows and tiles of the time below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L).
strategy.cx.cv: **Coefficient of variation.** The 2019 international consensus sets the target for glycemic variability at a coefficient of variation (%CV) of 36% or less (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2), a value it takes from Monnier et al. (2017). The ADA Standards of Care list the same goal of 36% or less ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). This explains the target in the CV row.
strategy.cx.cv_primary: The 2017 international consensus states that "CV should be considered the primary measure of variability" and describes the standard deviation as "a key secondary glycemic variability measure" (Danne et al., 2017, Section 5, para. 11). This explains why the CV row carries the variability target; the 2019 consensus and the ADA Standards of Care publish no target for the standard deviation ({ada_a}, Table 6.2; Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2).
strategy.cx.cv_stable: The 2017 international consensus defines stable glucose levels as a CV below 36% and unstable glucose levels as a CV of 36% or higher (Danne et al., 2017, Section 5). The 2019 consensus target is a CV of 36% or less (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2), so a CV of exactly 36% meets the 2019 target and is in the 2017 unstable range. This explains where the 36% value in the CV row comes from; GlucoCraft compares the CV with the 2019 target (GlucoCraft rule, following the treatment standards).
strategy.cx.dagger: The 2019 international consensus states that "each incremental 5% increase in TIR is associated with clinically significant benefits" for people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3 note); 5 percentage points are 1 hour and 12 minutes per day. This explains the ‡ mark, which flags a difference of 5 percentage points or more in either direction between the two periods compared (GlucoCraft rule), and is not an assessment. For clinical trials, the 2023 international consensus statement considers a difference of 5 percentage points in time in range clinically meaningful for an individual participant (Battelino et al., 2023, Panel 4).
strategy.cx.enough: **Data sufficiency.** The ADA Standards of Care list two conditions for valid CGM data: at least 14 days of wear, and the CGM active for 70% of the time over those 14 days ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). The 2019 international consensus gives the same 14 days and 70%, counted as a share of the possible CGM readings (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). For this reason, ✓ / ✗ and green / red are shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active; GlucoCraft measures *sensor active* as the share of the period represented by the readings received (GlucoCraft rule).
strategy.cx.forms: The 2019 international consensus describes a single-page report as of value and states that more detailed reports, for example detailed daily reports, "should remain available for individualized review" (Battelino et al., 2019, Standardization of CGM Data Presentation section, para. 2). The ADA Standards of Care recommend a minimum of a single-page report, such as the standardized CGM report and a weekly summary, and state that options for daily and weekly reports and raw data should be available ({ada_b}, Recommendation 7.9). This explains why the CGM Report has a summary and a full report with daily profiles, a daily summary and an hourly log, and why the readings can be exported as CSV.
strategy.cx.gmi: **Glucose management indicator (GMI).** The ADA Standards of Care describe GMI as a "calculated value approximating A1C (not always equivalent)" and state, for mean glucose and GMI, that "goals for these values are not standardized" ({ada_a}, Table 6.2); A1C (glycated hemoglobin) is measured by a laboratory blood test. This explains why the GMI row is marked "not a laboratory A1C" and has no consensus target.
strategy.cx.gmi_days: Bergenstal et al. (2018), who introduced GMI, suggest that "at least 10 and preferably 14 or more days of CGM data" be used to calculate it (Bergenstal et al., 2018, How Is GMI Calculated? section, para. 5). This explains why GMI is shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active.
strategy.cx.gmi_formula: Bergenstal et al. (2018) calculate GMI from the mean CGM glucose as GMI (%) = 3.31 + 0.02392 × mean glucose in mg/dL, a formula derived from 528 people in four randomized trials (Bergenstal et al., 2018, How Is GMI Calculated? section, Figure 1). This explains how the GMI value is calculated.
strategy.cx.gri: **Glycemia Risk Index.** Klonoff et al. (2023) define a hypoglycemia component, the percentage of time below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) plus 0.8 × the percentage at 54–69 mg/dL (3.0–3.8 mmol/L), and a hyperglycemia component, the percentage above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) plus 0.5 × the percentage at 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L); the GRI is 3.0 × the hypoglycemia component + 1.6 × the hyperglycemia component, capped at 100 (Klonoff et al., 2023, Development of the GRI section). They state that the two components "should be calculated and displayed separately" (Klonoff et al., 2023, Abstract, para. 3). This explains the GRI value and the separate hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia values beside it. Klonoff et al. (2023) describe the GRI as "not a substitute for looking at individual metrics" but as a summary score (Klonoff et al., 2023, Limitations section, para. 2). This explains why the GRI is shown together with the time-in-range values from which it is calculated, not in place of them.
strategy.cx.groups: **Other groups.** The consensus also publishes different targets for some groups, such as older or high-risk adults and pregnancy (Battelino et al., 2019, Tables 3 and 4: [the published article](https://doi.org/10.2337/dci19-0028)). They are not included here. The results here are calculated with the ranges and targets for adults in general, not with the ranges for these groups.
strategy.cx.limits: **The two limits.** The ADA Standards of Care state that 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) "has been recognized as a threshold for adrenergic responses to falling glucose in people without diabetes" and that level 2, below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L), "is the threshold at which neuroglycopenic symptoms begin to occur" ({ada_a}, Hypoglycemia Definitions and Event Rates section, para. 1). This explains the two limits of the rows of the time below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L).
strategy.cx.names: **Names of the ranges.** The 2019 international consensus names the glucose ranges of the standardized report "Very High" (level 2), "High" (level 1), "Low" (level 1) and "Very Low" (level 2) (Battelino et al., 2019, Standardization of CGM Data Presentation section, para. 1). This explains the range names Very high, High, Low and Very low.
strategy.cx.per_day: **Time per day.** The 2019 international consensus states that the times in ranges can be reported as a percentage, as hours and minutes per day, or both (Battelino et al., 2019, Time in Ranges section); a published guide to the standardized report rounds each 1% to about 15 minutes (HealthPartners Institute International Diabetes Center, 2024c, p. 2). This explains the time per day shown with each percentage of the periods of 24 hours or longer; GlucoCraft calculates it exactly, as 1% = 14.4 minutes (GlucoCraft rule).
strategy.cx.tight: **Time in tight range.** The 2017 international consensus on the use of CGM lists 70–140 mg/dL (3.9–7.8 mmol/L) as a secondary target range (Danne et al., 2017). The 2023 international consensus statement for clinical trials calls the time in this range *time in tight range* and, for clinical trials that use it, suggests a target of more than 70% (Battelino et al., 2023). The 2019 consensus for clinical care and the ADA Standards of Care set no target for it ({ada_a}; Battelino et al., 2019). For this reason, the Time in Tight Range row has no target and is shown without green or red.
strategy.cx.tir: **Time in range (TIR).** The 2019 international consensus sets the time-in-range target at more than 70% of the time at 70–180 mg/dL (3.9–10.0 mmol/L), which is more than 16 hours and 48 minutes per day (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3). The ADA Standards of Care state that a goal of more than 70% time in range is appropriate for many nonpregnant adults using CGM ({ada_a}, Recommendation 6.3b). This explains the target in the Time in Range row, tile and headline.
strategy.cx.trend: Abbott Diabetes Care (2022) describes trend arrows that show the direction in which glucose is heading: rising or falling quickly, more than 2 mg/dL per minute; rising or falling, between 1 and 2 mg/dL per minute; and changing slowly, less than 1 mg/dL per minute (Abbott Diabetes Care, 2022, p. 11). In mmol/L, 2 and 1 mg/dL per minute are 0.11 and 0.06 mmol/L per minute (converted by GlucoCraft). This explains the categories of the Trend arrow entity, which GlucoCraft applies to its own calculated rate of change for every CGM (GlucoCraft rule). GlucoCraft's arrow is calculated from smoothed readings, so it can lag behind the CGM system's own arrow.

strategy.note.reading_interval: GlucoCraft is designed for readings every 5 minutes or more often. With 15-minute or longer intervals, the trend arrow, the 5-minute delta, the no-current-data limit, gaps and sensor active are not designed to function as described; readings are still stored and shown.
strategy.note.sensor_limits: The sensor limits must match the CGM sensor's measurement range. GlucoCraft sets them from the source where it can and shows a Repairs notice when the readings point to a different limit; otherwise they are set by hand ([Documentation > Readings Outside the Sensor's Range]({lohi_url})). It is the user's responsibility to know their CGM system and to adjust these settings where necessary.

strategy.report.about:
- **Model:** The CGM Report shows the standardized metrics and glucose profile recommended for the Ambulatory Glucose Profile (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2013). Consensus ranges only (Battelino et al., 2019; tight range: Battelino et al., 2023), irrespective of the settings; the time-in-ranges colors of the published report examples (Battelino et al., 2019; HealthPartners Institute International Diabetes Center, 2024c).
- **Period:** full days ending at the last midnight: 14 days, 30 days, 90 days or 6 months. The first section always shows the most recent 14 days, the period recommended by the cited sources (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2013); a longer period adds the longer-term overview with consecutive 14-day periods.
- **PDF and Printing** (the box below the period and report selection): *Download PDF* creates the report (summary, or full with daily pages), in color or grayscale; the color setting applies to the PDF and the printout only. Each PDF is also kept in the folder `glucocraft_reports` of the Home Assistant configuration (the last 12), which is not accessible from the web.
- **Printing** (optional): with a printer address in GlucoCraft's settings, *Print Report* sends the PDF to a network printer that accepts PDF over the Internet Printing Protocol (IPP).
- **Laboratory A1C:** results entered here (or with the action `glucocraft.add_lab_a1c`) are compared with the GMI (Bergenstal et al., 2018) of the 90 days ending on each laboratory date; a result dated more than about 110 days ago has no CGM comparison (data older than 200 days are not kept). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
- **Previous period:** compared for 14, 30 and 90 days; the 6-month report has none, because it would require about 360 days of readings and GlucoCraft keeps 200 days.
- **Data:** `/api/glucocraft/report` and `/api/glucocraft/report.pdf` (Home Assistant login).
strategy.settings.about:
- **Effect of custom ranges:** the color and the zone word of the glucose value on the display cards and any wall panels change immediately; *Custom Ranges* (while the optional feature *Custom ranges and goals* is on) changes within 5 minutes. *Today*, *Consensus Ranges* and the *CGM Report* always use the consensus ranges.
- **No current data after** determines when the red banner appears on the dashboard and when the display cards and any wall panels show *No current data* in place of the value.
- **Weekly pages:** the nine weekly pages of the display card and of every wall panel use one of two range sets: the consensus ranges or the custom ranges (setting *Range set of the weekly pages*). The target line and the green and red background follow the range set shown, labeled *Consensus target* or *Custom goal*; pages without one are neutral gray. The dashboard shows the consensus ranges on *Consensus Ranges* and, while the optional feature *Custom ranges and goals* is on, the custom ranges on *Custom Ranges*.
- **Separate statistics entities:** one Home Assistant entity per statistic and period (mean glucose, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, lowest and highest reading, readings and sensor active; GMI and Glycemia Risk Index from 14 days), in addition to the period summaries; GlucoCraft's dashboard, display card and wall panels do not use them.
- **Wall-panel feed:** the local address (the wall-panel address) from which the wall panels download GlucoCraft's data; *on* while the address exists. No address exists after setup: the first one is created by ticking *Create a new wall-panel address* (screen *Display card and wall panels*) before the first wall panel is built, because the build needs its id. While no address exists, no panel receives data. After that, a new address is created only if the address may have been exposed (for example in a shared log, backup or screenshot); this at once stops every wall panel until each one is built and installed again with the new id.
strategy.settings.changing.heading: Changing Settings
strategy.settings.changing.steps:
1. Select **Change Settings** at the top of this page (or open **Settings > Devices & services > GlucoCraft**), then the gear icon (**Configure**) on the GlucoCraft row.
2. A menu lists the screens by topic: **Glucose sources** (the primary source, the CGM sensor expiry entity, the sensor lower and upper limit and the measurement-time attribute; the second source in a collapsed section; no-current-data interval); **Units and formats** (display unit, A1C and GMI unit, time and date formats, first day of the week, decimal separator); **Optional features** (*Custom ranges and goals* and *Separate statistics entities*, both off in a new installation); **Glucose ranges** (very low, low, tight range, high and very high, in the display unit) and **Custom goals** (the goals used on *Custom Ranges*; the explanation under each field gives the consensus value), both only while *Custom ranges and goals* is on; **Display card and wall panels** (card layout, *Trend shown as*, the seven display colors, the graph range colors in a collapsed section, the display card and wall panel backgrounds, *Outline text*, *Fade the words when there is no current reading*, the range set of the weekly pages while custom ranges or goals are in use, a new wall-panel address); **Notifications** (daily and weekly summaries, the no-data notice with *Notify after*, phones with *Send a test notification now*); and **Report and dashboard** (PDF paper size, report printer, dashboard in the sidebar, *When GlucoCraft is deleted*).
3. Select a screen, change the values and select **Submit**: that screen is saved on its own. **✕** closes a screen without saving.

To restore the consensus ranges, enter the values in the *Consensus default* column.

strategy.settings.requirements.heading: Requirements of Each Setting
strategy.settings.requirements.table:
| Setting | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Glucose source** | A Home Assistant sensor entity whose state is the glucose value in **mg/dL or mmol/L** with that unit as its unit of measurement (a value without a unit is read as mg/dL), updated with each new CGM reading. Preferably the entity also provides the measurement time as an attribute. {interval_note} A repair notice is raised when a source updates every 15 minutes or less often. |
| **Sensor lower limit / sensor upper limit** (each source) | The CGM sensor's measurement range: *Automatic* (the default) or, set by hand, lower 40 or 50 mg/dL (2.2 or 2.8 mmol/L) and upper 400, 450 or 500 mg/dL (22.2, 25.0 or 27.8 mmol/L). A reading beyond a limit is shown as LO or HI, left out of the calculated values and counted as very low or very high in the time in ranges. With a limit chosen by hand, a reading at the limit is LO or HI as well. {limit_note} |
| **Second source** (optional) | A second sensor entity for the same CGM, received through a **different path** (another cloud service or app); A second source is designed to supply readings that the primary source misses, up to 24 hours back, and to continue when it stops, merged by measurement time. The same unit rule applies. |
| **Measurement-time attribute** | An attribute containing a date and time or a time stamp. The Home Assistant clock must be correct. Without the attribute, readings are recorded at the time of receipt, and delivery delays shift them. |
| **Sensor-expiry entity** (optional) | An entity whose state is the sensor's expiry (date and time, date or time stamp) or the time remaining with a unit (days, hours, minutes). It must change when a new sensor is started; otherwise the warm-up cannot be detected. |
| **No current data after** | 5 to 30 minutes; default 15 minutes, the length of the gap rule. Longer than the usual delivery delay of the CGM data: at least three reading intervals plus any delay of the path that delivers them (for example a cloud service). A shorter interval produces false "no current data" states; a longer interval delays the indication of real gaps. |
| **Ranges** | Values in the display unit, in ascending order: very low less than low, low at most tight-range low, tight-range low less than tight-range high, tight-range high at most high, and high less than very high. {custom_statement} |
| **Display colors** | One color per range as a hex value (#RRGGBB); the default palette shows lows in red and highs in blue. Color is never the only cue: the zone word is shown under every value, and the zone is also published as text (attributes `zone` in every zone, `display_word` as shown, `zone_label` outside the range only). A second set of seven colors, the graph range colors, is used for the range bands of the graphs; by default they are the CGM Report's time-in-ranges colors. The CGM Report keeps the colors of the published report examples. |
| **Summaries** | The daily summary is on by default and the weekly summary off; each can be turned on or off in the settings. Home Assistant must be running at the time; a summary missed while Home Assistant was not running is not sent later. Summaries appear in Home Assistant (the bell). |
| **Notifications on a phone** (optional) | The phone selected under *Also send notifications to*, with the Home Assistant Companion app installed and signed in (required for the phone to be listed); notifications permitted for the app; battery optimization disabled for the app (on phones that offer it); a connection from the phone to Home Assistant or to the app's push service. Each message is an ordinary notification, with no priority, sound or channel of its own: the phone shows it according to its own notification settings. Messages may nevertheless be delayed or not delivered. |
| **No-data notice** (optional) | Home Assistant running and connected: the notice is created by Home Assistant itself, so it is not created while Home Assistant is not running, and a phone receives it only as described under *Notifications on a phone*. |
| **Wall panels** (optional) | A panel built from GlucoCraft's example panel configurations; the wall-panel address, created with *Create a new wall-panel address* before the first panel is built (the build needs its id); the panel on the same local network as Home Assistant (the example configurations connect over 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi); and a trusted network (see [Documentation > Privacy and Wall Panels]({privacy_url})). |
| **Weekly pages: custom ranges and goals** | Custom ranges or goals in the settings. The display card switches at the reload that follows the save; every wall panel downloads the files again about 15 seconds later. |
strategy.start.about:
- **GlucoCraft** is designed to calculate and display continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data provided by other systems. See [Documentation]({docs_url}).
- {readings}
- **This page.** The pages card lists the dashboard's pages; its *Custom Ranges* row is shown only while the optional feature *Custom ranges and goals* is on and custom ranges or custom goals are set. Its *Maintenance* button shows the Maintenance status: green with a wrench and *No issues*, or red with an alert icon and the number of issues, listed on the Maintenance page.
- **Ranges.** *Today*, *Consensus Ranges* and the *CGM Report* use the international consensus ranges 70–180, 54 and 250 mg/dL = 3.9–10.0, 3.0 and 13.9 mmol/L (Battelino et al., 2019); tight range 70–140 mg/dL = 3.9–7.8 mmol/L (Battelino et al., 2023). *Custom Ranges*, the display cards and any wall panels use the ranges in use: the ranges in the settings while the optional feature *Custom ranges and goals* is on, otherwise the consensus ranges (see [Settings Status]({settings_url})).
- **Display card colors.** The glucose value is colored by range, in the display colors in use (default palette: red shades below the range, green the tight range (Battelino et al., 2023), amber in range outside the tight range (Battelino et al., 2019), blue shades above the range). The range bands of the graphs use the graph range colors, by default the time-in-ranges colors of the CGM Report: dark red below the very-low limit, red low, green in range outside the tight range, light green the tight range, yellow high and orange very high. Both sets can be changed in the settings, screen *Display card and wall panels* (the graph range colors in its section *Graph range colors*). Color is never the only cue: under the value its range is named (Very low, Low, In range, Tight range, High, Very high), and the graphs show the range bands on a numbered axis. Status bar: green, a reading received within the *No current data after* interval (the bar shows its age); amber, sensor expiry within 24 hours (with an expiry entity); red, no current data or sensor expired; purple, sensor warm-up or no data received yet; gray, no status yet (while GlucoCraft is loading). An amber banner is shown while the second source is in use. The weekly pages say *Consensus target* or *Custom goal* where a target or goal colors the chart (see [Documentation > Ranges, Terminology and Colors]({ranges_url})).
- **Gaps.** A gap is an interval between two readings that is longer than 15 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer (in use: {gap_minutes} minutes), the reading interval being the median of the 10 intervals before the reading (the higher of the two middle values). Graphs are interrupted there, and percentages exclude it. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. A red banner is shown while there is no current data: the newest reading is older than the limit set under *No current data after* (in use: {no_data_minutes} minutes).
- **LO / HI.** A reading below the sensor's measurement range is shown as LO and a reading above it as HI (with a limit chosen by hand in the settings, a reading at that limit as well), never as a number, in the very-low or very-high color. It has no value: graphs show a gap with a row of small marks along the bottom (LO) or top (HI) edge, and the statistics count it as very low or very high in the time in ranges, leave it out of every value and state the time at the limit below each statistics table. This method is a GlucoCraft rule; see [Documentation > Readings Outside the Sensor's Range]({lohi_url}).

ui.change.note.consensus: Values of each 4-week period; --- for a period with less than 70% sensor active. The differences and the direction are calculated for every period with at least 70% sensor active; the sensor-active row shows the sensor active of each period that has enough data. Direction: whether the last 4 weeks are higher or lower than 22–26 weeks ago (or 9–13 weeks ago when 22–26 weeks ago has less than 70% sensor active), or no change when the difference rounds to zero; a numerical difference without clinical interpretation. ‡: a difference in time in range of 5 percentage points or more in either direction, beside the difference that the direction uses (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3 note); not an assessment. GMI is shown only for periods with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2018). Last 14 days: ✓ / ✗, an arithmetic comparison with the consensus target (Battelino et al., 2019), from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
ui.change.note.custom: Values of each 4-week period; --- for a period with less than 70% sensor active. The differences and the direction are calculated for every period with at least 70% sensor active; the sensor-active row shows the sensor active of each period that has enough data. Direction: whether the last 4 weeks are higher or lower than 22–26 weeks ago (or 9–13 weeks ago when 22–26 weeks ago has less than 70% sensor active), or no change when the difference rounds to zero; a numerical difference without clinical interpretation. GMI is shown only for periods with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2018). Last 14 days: ✓ / ✗, an arithmetic comparison with the custom goal, from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.

The line is interrupted at every gap: an interval between two readings that is longer than 15 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer, the reading interval being the median of the 10 intervals before the reading (the higher of the two middle values; the same rule as in the statistics and sensor active). This method is a GlucoCraft rule. A LO / HI reading has no value and interrupts the line.

ui.limit_note.rule: A reading at the sensor's limit gives no value, so it is left out of the mean, standard deviation, CV, GMI and the lowest and highest values, and it is counted as very low or very high in the time in ranges. No consensus document addresses such readings, and a CGM manufacturer's report software shows them at the limit (Abbott Diabetes Care, 2018), so these values can differ from such a report. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.

ui.statistics.attribution: All findings are attributed to their original authors; full references are on the Documentation page.
ui.statistics.gap_note: A gap is an interval between two readings that is longer than 15 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer, the reading interval being the median of the 10 intervals before the reading (the higher of the two middle values). Gaps are excluded from every value and from sensor active, and every graph is interrupted there. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
ui.statistics.group.consensus: Consensus Targets — ✓ Meets / ✗ Does Not Meet
ui.statistics.group.consensus_note: Consensus targets (Battelino et al., 2019); the context of each target is in About This Page.
ui.statistics.group.observational_note: Values observed in the CGM data. No consensus targets apply.
ui.statistics.group.supplementary_note: No consensus target for clinical care has been established for these metrics.
ui.statistics.last_reading_note: The most recent reading with its measurement time; its 5-minute delta, the change of the smoothed level (an adaptive mean of the most recent readings) over 5 minutes (calculated by GlucoCraft; shown only while there is current data); the source of the current value; and the sensor expiry (where configured). Data history: the longest statistics period that the span of the stored readings reaches (for example 14 Days); it does not show how much of that time has data, which the sensor-active row shows. This method is a GlucoCraft rule; Documentation, How GlucoCraft Is Designed, describes it. Trend arrow: calculated by GlucoCraft in the trend categories of Abbott Diabetes Care (2022) from smoothed readings, so it can lag behind the continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system's own arrow.
ui.statistics.note.cv: Standard deviation divided by the mean, as a percentage.
ui.statistics.note.gmi: An estimate of A1C (glycated hemoglobin, measured by a blood test) from CGM data: 3.31 + 0.02392 × mean glucose in mg/dL; in mmol/mol, 12.71 + 4.70587 × mean glucose in mmol/L (Bergenstal et al., 2018). Shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active; not a laboratory A1C; no standardized goal.
ui.statistics.note.gri: A composite score (0–100) of the hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia components (Klonoff et al., 2023). GRI is shown for periods of 14 days or more; shorter periods show ---. Unlike GMI, it is also shown with less than 70% sensor active. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. The CGM Report shows the GRI with its zone. Under each value: the hypoglycemia component · the hyperglycemia component.
ui.statistics.note.limit_readings: Readings outside the sensor's measurement range and the time they represent, left out of the values above (GlucoCraft rule; see the note below).
ui.statistics.note.mean: Time-weighted mean of the readings; GMI is calculated from it (Bergenstal et al., 2018).
ui.statistics.note.sensor_active: The share of the period represented by the readings received (GlucoCraft rule; see About This Page).
ui.statistics.note.tight_range: No target for clinical care; shown without green or red.
ui.statistics.periods_note.consensus: All statistics over seven rolling periods (6 hours to 6 months), on the consensus ranges (Battelino et al., 2019). ✓ green: meets the consensus target; ✗ red: does not meet it; an arithmetic comparison, not a clinical assessment, shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019); shorter periods are not compared. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. In the periods of 24 hours or longer, time-based rows include the time per day, in hours (h) and minutes (min) (1% = {minutes} minutes).
ui.statistics.periods_note.custom: All statistics over seven rolling periods (6 hours to 6 months), on the consensus ranges (Battelino et al., 2019); the custom ranges are used on Custom Ranges. ✓ green: meets the consensus target; ✗ red: does not meet it; an arithmetic comparison, not a clinical assessment, shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019); shorter periods are not compared. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. In the periods of 24 hours or longer, time-based rows include the time per day, in hours (h) and minutes (min) (1% = {minutes} minutes).

ui.statistics.said.no_data_since: No current data. Last reading {age} ago.
ui.stats.footnote.consensus: Colors and ✓ / ✗: an arithmetic comparison with the consensus target, not a clinical assessment, from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). GMI is shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2018). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
ui.stats.footnote.custom: Colors and ✓ / ✗: an arithmetic comparison with the custom goal, not a clinical assessment, from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). GMI is shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2018). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
ui.stats.footnote.per_day: Under each time percentage of a period of 24 hours or longer: its time per 24-hour day, in hours (h) and minutes (min); 1% = {minutes} minutes.
